classification.difficultyReason: Construct the three semicircle relationships, decompose the unlabelled lunes into semicircle areas minus shared circular segments, and select Pythagoras to cancel the squared-side terms. The area36 is given, but the multi-step decomposition and theorem connection are not scaffolded; no new theorem beyond the supplied circle-area and Pythagoras methods is required.

content.prompt:
Circles. Start with a right-angled triangle. Construct three circles, using the three sides as diameters so that each circle has the midpoint of a side as its centre, as shown. Assume that the area of the triangle is $36\text{ cm}^2$. Find the combined area of the shaded regions of the two smaller circles that lie outside the largest circle.

What is surprising about the result?

spec.description: Complete circles on three sides of a right triangle, vertical short leg left/horizontal longer leg below. Only two smaller-circle regions outside the hypotenuse circle shaded. Three side midpoint centres red, right-angle lower-left. No numeric dimensions supplied.
spec.mathematics: Right triangle and its diameter circles; the requested two lunes are mathematical fill, not decorative backgrounds.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied source regions/centres only, no derived area.

answer.short: $36\text{ cm}^2$, equal to the area of the triangle.
answer.worked:
Call the perpendicular sides $a,b$ and the hypotenuse $c$. The two outward semicircles have total area $\pi \frac{a^2}{8}+\pi \frac{b^2}{8}$. The semicircle on the hypotenuse, on the triangle side, consists of the triangle together with the two unshaded circular segments. Thus the two lunes have combined area

$$\begin{aligned}L&=\frac{\pi a^2}{8}+\frac{\pi b^2}{8}-\left(\frac{\pi c^2}{8}-\frac{ab}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{\pi(a^2+b^2-c^2)}{8}+\frac{ab}{2}\\&=\frac{ab}{2}=36\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

The cancellation uses Pythagoras’ theorem, $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Surprisingly, the combined curved lune area equals the triangle area, independent of the right triangle’s shape.
